summary: The opt-in Main ordinary-assignment path independently verifies authoritative obligations, snapshot and decision, then binds actual work/principal, requested configuration, input, generation, reservation and original fixed budget. Bounded evidence is staged in the existing content-addressed store before immutable route and intent; semantic-assignment and object-byte digests survive route/4, command/6, resolver readback, chunk transfer and runner launch equality. Historical plain preparation preserves its canonical bytes, while ordinary and causal wrappers retain validated route bytes. Terminal replacement recovery requires the exact persisted launch, a bounded canonical versioned session receipt with checksum and original inspector command identity, and a matching verified artifact. Duplicate launch and reconciliation recover the original terminal session without another provider invocation; terminal cancellation reports already terminal. Missing, corrupt or changed terminal proof retains reconciliation uncertainty, including historical records lacking the new receipt; spawn intent alone proves no terminal outcome. Unsupported launch tools/checks/resources and missing or changed assignment evidence refuse. Retained configuration and provenance remain supplied evidence rather than authenticated provider observations. Deferred output and independent review obligations hold native outcome acceptance. Focused fixtures cover byte compatibility, one invocation, terminal/session replay, corrupt or missing receipts, artifact-origin drift and missing terminal state. Actual real-PostgreSQL positive/crash/lifecycle execution, required exact-head CI and protected delivery remain separate evidence gates. This source does not establish installed matched Host/Runner adoption, preventive isolation, runtime containment, complete framework/Python-JavaScript journeys, parent acceptance or economic effectiveness.
title: Ordinary assignment durable Main and runner source boundary
